# hprof-analyzer

Rust CLI + MCP server for Java heap dump analysis. Investigates OutOfMemoryErrors and memory leaks in JVM applications by parsing `.hprof` files. Generates MAT-parity reports (leak suspects, retained-size breakdown, OQL queries) with peak RSS well below the dump size.

> Built by the [SapMachine](https://sapmachine.io) team. MIT licensed.

## What this tool does

- Parses `.hprof`, `.hprof.gz`, `.hprof.zip` heap dumps from HotSpot, OpenJ9, and Android ART
- Builds a dominator tree, computes retained sizes, identifies leak suspects and top consumers
- Runs SQL-flavoured OQL queries (Eclipse MAT-compatible dialect with extensions)
- Exposes all of the above via an MCP server for AI assistant integration
- Generates Eclipse MAT-compatible cache files (lower RSS than MAT itself)
- Redacts sensitive values from heap dumps before sharing

## How to use as an AI assistant

### Option 1 — MCP server (recommended)

Register the MCP server once, then use structured tools to load dumps, run queries, and browse results.

**Claude Code:**
```sh
claude mcp add hprof -- hprof-analyzer mcp
```

**Claude Desktop** (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hprof": { "command": "hprof-analyzer", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

**Cline / VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`):
```json
{
  "hprof": { "command": "hprof-analyzer", "args": ["mcp"] }
}
```

#### MCP tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_session_info` | Check if a dump is loaded |
| `load_dump` | Load a dump file (fast from cache after first run) |
| `get_report` | Structured report or named section: `triage` ⭐, `leaks`, `top-classes`, `top-objects`, `threads`, `overview` |
| `get_histogram` | Class histogram |
| `query` | Run OQL or a built-in view by name |
| `browse_dominators` | Navigate the dominator tree |
| `inspect_object` | Details for a specific object |
| `get_oql_docs` | OQL language reference (no dump needed) |
| `redact` | Zero primitive values before sharing |

#### MCP investigation workflow

```
1. load_dump({path: "/abs/path/to/heap.hprof"})
2. get_report({section: "triage"})     ⭐ — severity-tagged signals, fastest orientation
3. get_report({section: "leaks"})         — root paths, accumulation points
4. get_histogram                          — class-level breakdown
5. query({oql: "..."})                    — drill in with OQL
6. browse_dominators                      — walk the dominator tree
```

### Option 2 — CLI fallback (no MCP needed)

If you cannot register an MCP server, use the `heap` subcommand group. It caches results on the first run; all subsequent calls return in ~1 s.

```sh
# First orientation
hprof-analyzer heap summary heap.hprof

# Severity-tagged signals (fastest diagnosis)
hprof-analyzer heap report heap.hprof --section triage

# Leak suspects with root paths
hprof-analyzer heap report heap.hprof --section leaks

# OQL query
hprof-analyzer heap query heap.hprof --oql "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM java.lang.String"

# Browse dominator tree
hprof-analyzer heap browse heap.hprof

# Inspect a specific object (index from query @objectId column)
hprof-analyzer heap inspect heap.hprof --index 42
```

Add `--json` to any `heap` subcommand for machine-readable output.

Available `--section` values: `triage`, `leaks`, `top`, `threads`, `overview`, `waste`, `indicators`, `retainers`, `arrays`, `collections`, `references`, `dominators`, `components`, `alloc_sites`, `thread_locals`, `framework`, `field_stats`, `all`.

**Important:** use `heap query` (not the `query` subcommand) for queries that need `@retainedHeapSize` or dominator attributes — the `query` subcommand does a fast streaming parse only.

## Install

```sh
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew tap parttimenerd/hprof-analyzer
brew trust parttimenerd/hprof-analyzer
brew install hprof-analyzer

# macOS (Apple Silicon, direct)
curl -L https://github.com/parttimenerd/hprof-analyzer/releases/download/nightly/hprof-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | tar xz
sudo mv hprof-analyzer-*/hprof-analyzer /usr/local/bin/

# Linux x86_64
curl -L https://github.com/parttimenerd/hprof-analyzer/releases/download/nightly/hprof-analyzer-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | tar xz
sudo mv hprof-analyzer-*/hprof-analyzer /usr/local/bin/

# Cargo (requires Rust 1.85+)
cargo install hprof-analyzer
```

| Path | Contents |
